rows.question: Why couldn't Apollo 13's command module CO2 canisters be used directly in the lunar module?
rows.expected: The command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round.
rows.answer:
The fact lines answer this directly. The command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square while the lunar module's were round, so they did not fit the lunar module's scrubber housing (src: co2-scrubber-adapter, NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24). Engineers at Mission Control Houston devised an adapter from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape, and the crew built it from radioed instructions (src: co2-scrubber-adapter; mission-control-houston, NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24).

The mismatch in shape is the stated reason. The fact lines do not say more about why the two canister designs differed, so I can't add further detail from them.

rows.question: Why did the Apollo Guidance Computer keep flying through the Apollo 11 alarms?
rows.expected: An agent concluded it was the software's priority scheduling; this is a derived inference, not a stated fact.
rows.answer:
The lines contain a claim that the software's priority scheduling is why the computer kept flying through the alarms, but it is tagged [derived] and attributed only to "agent" (margaret-hamilton, 2026-10-24). I can't confirm it from stated facts.

What the stated facts do say:
- The computer raised five program alarms during the powered descent, the first about 5 minutes after descent initiation (program-alarms-1201-1202; apollo-guidance-computer; apollo-11-mission-report-ch-05).
- The alarms did not degrade any primary guidance or control function, though they interfered with the crew's early assessment of the approach (program-alarms-1201-1202).
- Throttle reduction occurred at 386 seconds against 384 predicted, indicating nominal engine performance (apollo-11-mission-report-ch-05).

So the stated record supports that the alarms did not stop guidance, but the specific mechanism (priority scheduling) is an inference [derived], not a sourced fact.

rows.question: What happened at Launch Complex 34 on 1967-01-27?

A cabin fire during a launch rehearsal test on 1967-01-27 killed Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee. It happened at Launch Complex 34 at Cape Kennedy, and it led to a command module redesign that included a quick-opening hatch. (apollo-1)

rows.question: Which company's revised specification set the voltage that the Apollo 13 tank switches could not handle?
rows.expected: North American Aviation, which revised the heater specification to 65 volts in 1965; the switches were built for 28 volts.
rows.answer:
The question asks which company's revised specification set the voltage that the tank switches could not handle.

From the lines: the heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts by North American Aviation, while the thermostatic switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC and were never changed (oxygen-tank-2; north-american-aviation). Beech Aircraft built the tank and also did not change the switches when the spec moved to 65 volts (beech-aircraft).

Answer: North American Aviation (north-american-aviation) revised the heater specification to 65 volts, which the tank's switches could not handle (oxygen-tank-2).

rows.question: What was Apollo 13's mission goal before it changed, what changed it, and when?
rows.expected: A lunar landing at Fra Mauro; it became a safe return to Earth on 1970-04-13, by Mission Control's abort decision.
rows.answer:
The mission goal before the change was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro. It was changed to a safe return to Earth on 1970-04-13 by a Mission Control abort decision, after the oxygen tank exploded. (apollo-13)

What changed it was the explosion of Oxygen tank No. 2, about 56 hours into the flight on 1970-04-13. The Apollo 13 Review Board traced it to an electrically started fire in that tank. (oxygen-tank-2; apollo-13-review-board)

[derived] The Fra Mauro landing was abandoned because the service module's power and oxygen were lost, so the crew could not safely continue toward a landing; they used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and regained a free-return path with a descent engine burn. (apollo-13; lunar-module; free-return-trajectory)

rows.question: What was Jack Swigert's Apollo 13 role before 1970-04-10, and what is it now?

Jack Swigert's Apollo 13 role before 1970-04-10 was backup command module pilot. It is now prime command module pilot, a change made at the KSC management meeting on 1970-04-10 (jack-swigert; apollo-13; rubella-crew-swap).

He replaced Ken Mattingly, who was removed from the crew after blood tests showed he had no rubella immunity (ken-mattingly; rubella-crew-swap).

[derived] The swap was made because Mattingly could have fallen ill alone in the command module, so the change was about measles exposure rather than flight readiness.
